messages.content: You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

Please solve this issue: Times in the app are rendered by the server, in the server's timezone. That's
wrong for anyone anywhere else, and it kills page caching: everyone's clock
ends up baked into HTML we'd like to share between people.

Move time rendering into the browser, everywhere we show a date or time. The
server sends the raw timestamp; the page turns it into words in the viewer's
own timezone. A comment from two hours ago reads "1:42 PM"; one from last
night reads "yesterday"; one from earlier in the week reads "5 days ago" or
"Sep 12"; a card auto-closing overnight reads "tomorrow", further out "in 3
days".

{
  "returncode": 0,
  "output": "# Fizzy

Guidance for AI coding agents working with this repository.

Fizzy is a kanban-style project management and issue tracker: cards move across columns on boards, with comments, mentions, and assignments.

## Deploy

Default branch: `main`

Self-hosted deploys run Kamal against `config/deploy.yml` — see `docs/kamal-deployment.md`.

## SaaS mode

For local agent work, `tmp/saas.txt` is the checkout-level SaaS switch used by `bin/setup`. When present, read `saas/AGENTS.md` before continuing. Otherwise, do not apply its instructions.

## Architecture Overview

### Multi-Tenancy (URL-Based)

Fizzy uses **URL path-based multi-tenancy**:
- Accounts have a unique decimal `external_account_id` used in URL prefixes
- URLs are prefixed: `/{account_id}/boards/...`
- Middleware (`AccountSlug::Extractor`) extracts the account ID from the URL and sets `Current.account`
- The slug is moved from `PATH_INFO` to `SCRIPT_NAME`, making Rails think it's "mounted" at that path
- Tenant-scoped domain records are account-isolated; global identity, session, and authentication records are exceptions
- Background jobs automatically serialize and restore account context

**Key insight**: This architecture allows multi-tenancy without subdomains or separate databases, making local development and testing simpler.

### Authentication & Authorization

Passwordless magic link authentication. A global `Identity` (email-based) can have `Users` in multiple Accounts, so an email is not a single account membership. Users have roles: owner, admin, member, system. Board-level access control via `Access` records.

### Entropy System

Cards automatically "postpone" (move to "not now") after inactivity:
- Account-level default entropy period
- Board-level entropy override
- Prevents endless todo lists from accumulating
- Configurable via Account/Board settings

### UUID Primary Keys

All tables use UUIDs (UUIDv7 format, base36-encoded as 25-char strings):
- Custom fixture UUID generation maintains deterministic ordering for tests
- Fixtures are always "older" than runtime records
- `.first`/`.last` work correctly in tests

### Background Jobs (Solid Queue)

Database-backed job queue (no Redis):
- Custom `FizzyActiveJobExtensions` prepended to ActiveJob
- Jobs automatically capture/restore `Current.account`
- Mission Control::Jobs for monitoring

Recurring tasks are declared in `config/recurring.yml`.

### Sharded Full-Text Search

Full-text search runs in the database, not Elasticsearch. On MySQL it is sharded 16 ways by CRC32 of the account ID (`Search::Record::Trilogy`); on SQLite it is a single FTS5 index (`Search::Record::SQLite`). Don't assume the sharded shape when working under SQLite. Models in `app/models/search/`.

### Imports and exports

Allow people to move between OSS and SAAS Fizzy instances:
- Exports/Imports can be written to/read from local or S3 storage depending on the config of the instance (both must be supported)
- Must be able to handle very large ZIP files (500+GB)
- Models in `app/models/account/data_transfer/`, `app/models/zip_file`

## Coding style

Before editing or reviewing code, read STYLE.md.
=== STYLE.md ===

# Style

We aim to write code that is a pleasure to read, and we have a lot of opinions about how to do it well. Writing great code is an essential part of our programming culture, and we deliberately set a high bar for every code change anyone contributes. We care about how code reads, how code looks, and how code makes you feel when you read it.

We love discussing code. If you have questions about how to write something, or if you detect some smell you are not quite sure how to solve, please ask away to other programmers. A Pull Request is a great way to do this.

When writing new code, unless you are very familiar with our approach, try to find similar code elsewhere to look for inspiration.

## Conditional returns

In general, we prefer to use expanded conditionals over guard clauses.

```ruby
# Bad
def todos_for_new_group
  ids = params.require(:todolist)[:todo_ids]
  return [] unless ids
  @bucket.recordings.todos.find(ids.split(","))
end

# Good
def todos_for_new_group
  if ids = params.require(:todolist)[:todo_ids]
    @bucket.recordings.todos.find(ids.split(","))
  else
    []
  end
end
```

This is because guard clauses can be hard to read, especially when they are nested.

As an exception, we sometimes use guard clauses to return early from a method:

* When the return is right at the beginning of the method.
* When the main method body is not trivial and involves several lines of code.

```ruby
def after_recorded_as_commit(recording)
  return if recording.parent.was_created?

  if recording.was_created?
    broadcast_new_column(recording)
  else
    broadcast_column_change(recording)
  end
end
```

## Methods ordering

We order methods in classes in the following order:

1. `class` methods
2. `public` methods with `initialize` at the top.
3. `private` methods

## Invocation order

We order methods vertically based on their invocation order. This helps us to understand the flow of the code.

```ruby
class SomeClass
  def some_method
    method_1
    method_2
  end

  private
    def method_1
      method_1_1
      method_1_2
    end
  
    def method_1_1
      # ...
    end
  
    def method_1_2
      # ...
    end
  
    def method_2
      method_2_1
      method_2_2
    end
  
    def method_2_1
      # ...
    end
  
    def method_2_2
      # ...
    end
end
```

## To bang or not to bang

Should I call a method `do_something` or `do_something!`?

As a general rule, we only use `!` for methods that have a correspondent counterpart without `!`. In particular, we don’t use `!` to flag destructive actions. There are plenty of destructive methods in Ruby and Rails that do not end with `!`.

## Visibility modifiers

We don't add a newline under visibility modifiers, and we indent the content under them.

```ruby
class SomeClass
  def some_method
    # ...
  end

  private
    def some_private_method_1
      # ...
    end

    def some_private_method_2
      # ...
    end
end
```

If a module only has private methods, we mark it `private` at the top and add an extra new line after but don't indent.

```ruby
module SomeModule
  private
  
  def some_private_method
    # ...
  end
end
```

## CRUD controllers

We model web endpoints as CRUD operations on resources (REST). When an action doesn't map cleanly to a standard CRUD verb, we introduce a new resource rather than adding custom actions.

```ruby
# Bad
resources :cards do
  post :close
  post :reopen
end

# Good
resources :cards do
  resource :closure
end
```

## Controller and model interactions

In general, we favor a [vanilla Rails](https://dev.37signals.com/vanilla-rails-is-plenty/) approach with thin controllers directly invoking a rich domain model. We don't use services or other artifacts to connect the two.

Invoking plain Active Record operations is totally fine:

```ruby
class Cards::CommentsController < ApplicationController
  def create
    @comment = @card.comments.create!(comment_params)
  end
end
```

For more complex behavior, we prefer clear, intention-revealing model APIs that controllers call directly:

```ruby
class Cards::GoldnessesController < ApplicationController
  def create
    @card.gild
  end
end
```

When justified, it is fine to use services or form objects, but don't treat those as special artifacts:

```ruby
Signup.new(email_address: email_address).create_identity
```

## Run async operations in jobs

As a general rule, we write shallow job classes that delegate the logic itself to domain models:

* We typically use the suffix `_later` to flag methods that enqueue a job.
* A common scenario is having a model class that enqueues a job that, when executed, invokes some method in that same class. In this case, we use the suffix `_now` for the regular synchronous method.

```ruby
module Event::Relaying
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    after_create_commit :relay_later
  end

  def relay_later
    Event::RelayJob.perform_later(self)
  end

  def relay_now
    # ...
  end
end

class Event::RelayJob < ApplicationJob
  def perform(event)
    event.relay_now
  end
end
```

For more complex behavior, we prefer clear, intention-revealing model APIs that controllers call directly:

```ruby
class Cards::GoldnessesController < ApplicationController
  def create
    @card.gild
  end
end
```

When justified, it is fine to use services or form objects, but don't treat those as special artifacts:

```ruby
Signup.new(email_address: email_address).create_identity
```

## Run async operations in jobs

As a general rule, we write shallow job classes that delegate the logic itself to domain models:

* We typically use the suffix `_later` to flag methods that enqueue a job.
* A common scenario is having a model class that enqueues a job that, when executed, invokes some method in that same class. In this case, we use the suffix `_now` for the regular synchronous method.

```ruby
module Event::Relaying
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    after_create_commit :relay_later
  end

  def relay_later
    Event::RelayJob.perform_later(self)
  end

  def relay_now
    # ...
  end
end

class Event::RelayJob < ApplicationJob
  def perform(event)
    event.relay_now
  end
end
```

module FixturesTestHelper
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  class_methods do
    def identify(label, column_type = :integer)
      if label.to_s.end_with?("_uuid")
        column_type = :uuid
        label = label.to_s.delete_suffix("_uuid")
      end

      # Rails passes :string for varchar columns, so handle both :uuid and :string
      return super(label, column_type) unless column_type.in?([ :uuid, :string ])
      generate_fixture_uuid(label)
    end

    private

    def generate_fixture_uuid(label)
      # Generate deterministic UUIDv7 for fixtures that sorts by fixture ID
      # This allows .first/.last to work as expected in tests
      # Use the same CRC32 algorithm as Rails' default fixture ID generation
      # so that UUIDs sort in the same order as integer IDs
      fixture_int = Zlib.crc32("fixtures/#{label}") % (2**30 - 1)

      # Translate the deterministic order into times in the past, so that records
      # created during test runs are also always newer than the fixtures.
      base_time = Time.utc(2024, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0)
      timestamp = base_time + (fixture_int / 1000.0)

      uuid_v7_with_timestamp(timestamp, label)
    end

    def uuid_v7_with_timestamp(time, seed_string)
      # Generate UUIDv7 with custom timestamp and deterministic random bits
      # Format: 48-bit timestamp_ms | 12-bit sub_ms_precision | 4-bit version | 62-bit random

      time_ms = time.to_f * 1000
      timestamp_ms = time_ms.to_i

      # 48-bit timestamp (milliseconds since epoch)
      bytes = []
      bytes[0] = (timestamp_ms >> 40) & 0xff
      bytes[1] = (timestamp_ms >> 32) & 0xff
      bytes[2] = (timestamp_ms >> 24) & 0xff
      bytes[3] = (timestamp_ms >> 16) & 0xff
      bytes[4] = (timestamp_ms >> 8) & 0xff
      bytes[5] = timestamp_ms & 0xff

      # Use the 12-bit rand_a field for sub-millisecond precision

  belongs_to :account, default: -> { user.account }
  belongs_to :user

  enum :bundle_email_frequency, %i[ never every_few_hours daily weekly ],
    default: :every_few_hours, prefix: :bundle_email

  after_update :review_pending_bundles, if: :saved_change_to_bundle_email_frequency?

  def bundle_aggregation_period
    case bundle_email_frequency
    when "every_few_hours"
      4.hours
    when "daily"
      1.day
    when "weekly"
      1.week
    else
      1.day
    end
  end

module PaginationHelper
  def pagination_frame_tag(namespace, page, data: {}, **attributes, &)
    turbo_frame_tag pagination_frame_id_for(namespace, page.number), data: { timeline_target: "frame", **data }, role: "presentation", **attributes, &
  end

  def link_to_next_page(namespace, page, activate_when_observed: false, label: default_pagination_label(activate_when_observed), data: {}, **attributes)
    if page.before_last? && !params[:previous]
      attributes[:class] = class_names(attributes[:class], "btn txt-small center-block center": !activate_when_observed)
      pagination_link(namespace, page.number + 1, label: label, activate_when_observed: activate_when_observed, data: data, **attributes)
    end
  end

  def pagination_link(namespace, page_number, activate_when_observed: false, label: default_pagination_label(activate_when_observed), url_params: {}, data: {}, **attributes)
    link_to label, url_for(params.permit!.to_h.merge(page: page_number, **url_params)),
      "aria-label": "Load page #{page_number}",
      id: "#{namespace}-pagination-link-#{page_number}",
      class: class_names(attributes.delete(:class), "pagination-link", { "pagination-link--active-when-observed" => activate_when_observed }),
      data: {
        frame: pagination_frame_id_for(namespace, page_number),
        pagination_target: "paginationLink",
        action: ("click->pagination#loadPage:prevent" unless activate_when_observed),
        **data
      },
      **attributes
  end

  def pagination_frame_id_for(namespace, page_number)
    "#{namespace}-pagination-contents-#{page_number}"
  end

  def with_manual_pagination(name, page, **properties)
    pagination_list name, **properties do
      concat(pagination_frame_tag(name, page) do
        yield
        concat link_to_next_page(name, page)
      end)
    end
  end

  def with_automatic_pagination(name, page, **properties)
    pagination_list name, paginate_on_scroll: true, **properties do
      concat(pagination_frame_tag(name, page) do
        yield
        concat link_to_next_page(name, page, activate_when_observed: true)
      end)
    end
  end

  def day_timeline_pagination_frame_tag(day_timeline, &)
    turbo_frame_tag day_timeline_pagination_frame_id_for(day_timeline.day), data: { timeline_target: "frame" }, role: "presentation", refresh: :morph, &
  end

  def day_timeline_pagination_frame_id_for(day)
    "day-timeline-pagination-contents-#{day.strftime("%Y-%m-%d")}"
  end

  def day_timeline_pagination_link(day_timeline, filter)
    if day_timeline.next_day
      link_to "Load more…", events_days_path(day: day_timeline.next_day.strftime("%Y-%m-%d"), **filter.as_params),
        class: "day-timeline-pagination-link", data: { frame: day_timeline_pagination_frame_id_for(day_timeline.next_day), pagination_target: "paginationLink" }
    end
  end

  private
    def pagination_list(name, tag_element: :div, paginate_on_scroll: false, **properties, &block)
      classes = properties.delete(:class)
      properties[:id] ||= "#{name}-pagination-list"
      tag.public_send tag_element,
        class: token_list(name, "display-contents", classes),
        data: { controller: "pagination", pagination_paginate_on_intersection_value: paginate_on_scroll },
        **properties,
        &block
    end

    def default_pagination_label(activate_when_observed)
      "Load more…"
    end
end

        frame: pagination_frame_id_for(namespace, page_number),
        pagination_target: "paginationLink",
        action: ("click->pagination#loadPage:prevent" unless activate_when_observed),
        **data
      },
      **attributes
  end

  def pagination_frame_id_for(namespace, page_number)
    "#{namespace}-pagination-contents-#{page_number}"
  end

  def with_manual_pagination(name, page, **properties)
    pagination_list name, **properties do
      concat(pagination_frame_tag(name, page) do
        yield
        concat link_to_next_page(name, page)
      end)
    end
  end

  def with_automatic_pagination(name, page, **properties)
    pagination_list name, paginate_on_scroll: true, **properties do
      concat(pagination_frame_tag(name, page) do
        yield
        concat link_to_next_page(name, page, activate_when_observed: true)
      end)
    end
  end

  def day_timeline_pagination_frame_tag(day_timeline, &)
    turbo_frame_tag day_timeline_pagination_frame_id_for(day_timeline.day), data: { timeline_target: "frame" }, role: "presentation", refresh: :morph, &
  end

  def day_timeline_pagination_frame_id_for(day)
    "day-timeline-pagination-contents-#{day.strftime("%Y-%m-%d")}"
  end

    if day_timeline.next_day

    end
  end

    def pagination_list(name, tag_element: :div, paginate_on_scroll: false, **properties, &block)

      tag.public_send tag_element,
        class: token_list(name, "display-contents", classes),

    end

require "application_system_test_case"

class CardRefreshTest < ApplicationSystemTestCase
  include ActionView::RecordIdentifier

  setup do
    sign_in_as(users(:david))
    Current.user = users(:kevin)
    @card = cards(:layout)
  end

  test "a broadcast refresh shows card changes made elsewhere" do
    visit card_url(@card)
    assert_selector "h1", text: @card.title

    update_card_elsewhere

    assert_selector "h1", text: "Retitled elsewhere", wait: 5
    assert_text "Description updated elsewhere"
  end

  test "a broadcast refresh preserves an edit in progress" do
    visit card_url(@card)
    click_on @card.title

    within_edit_frame do
      fill_in_lexxy with: "Draft description in progress"
    end

    update_card_elsewhere

    # The title change's system comment appearing proves the refresh reached the page.
    assert_text "changed the title", wait: 5
    within_edit_frame do
      assert_selector "lexxy-editor", text: "Draft description in progress"
    end
    assert_no_text "Description updated elsewhere"
  end

  test "canceling an edit reveals card changes made elsewhere during the edit" do
    visit card_url(@card)
    click_on @card.title
    within_edit_frame { assert_selector "form" }

    update_card_elsewhere
    assert_text "changed the title", wait: 5

    send_keys :escape

    assert_selector "h1", text: "Retitled elsewhere"
    assert_text "Description updated elsewhere"
  end

  test "a broadcast refresh shows card changes after an edit is canceled" do
    visit card_url(@card)
    click_on @card.title
    within_edit_frame { assert_selector "form" }

    send_keys :escape
    assert_selector "a.card__title-link", text: @card.title

    update_card_elsewhere

    assert_selector "h1", text: "Retitled elsewhere", wait: 5
    assert_text "Description updated elsewhere"
  end

  private
    def update_card_elsewhere
      wait_for_cable_subscriptions
      @card.update!(title: "Retitled elsewhere", description: "Description updated elsewhere")
      perform_enqueued_jobs only: Turbo::Streams::BroadcastStreamJob
    end

    # A broadcast sent before the page's subscriptions are confirmed is lost.
    def wait_for_cable_subscriptions
      assert_selector "turbo-cable-stream-source[connected]", visible: :all
      assert_no_selector "turbo-cable-stream-source:not([connected])", visible: :all
    end

    def within_edit_frame(&block)
      within "##{dom_id(@card, :edit)}", &block
    end
end

    end

Okay, this is becoming clearer. I'm seeing a deep-seated issue with how time is handled across the application, especially in relation to caching and user timezones. My initial thought process led me to investigate `CurrentTimezone`, its usage, and its interaction with various components that render time-related data. I need to be *sure* I understand where everything is used.

I'm seeing instances where `Time.zone` is being used in request-scoped contexts via `CurrentTimezone`, influencing how dates and times are parsed and displayed. However, this is also seeping into cached partials (like cards, comments, notifications, and day timelines), leading to time values being "baked" into the HTML at render time. This is a problem because, as the prompt states, this breaks the page caching. The time rendered is based on *the server's* timezone, not the user's. This means that after the page caches, everyone sees the time from the first user to access the page!

I identified that in several instances (`time_ago_in_words`, `strftime` calls), time-related data is being directly rendered into the HTML. This means that cached content is not updated dynamically based on the current user's timezone. The `date_helpers.js` file, coupled with the `<meta name="timezone">` tag, seems like an attempt to reconcile the server-rendered time with the client's timezone, but I need to investigate how this is used and if it's currently correct. I need to know how these relate to caching.

The real "a-ha" moment is the realization that the prompt is *very* specific about how time should be handled: sending *raw timestamps* from the server, and rendering the time in the *browser* using the user's timezone. The CSS classes (`.local-time-value`, `local-time`) and the inclusion of `TimeHelper` in `User::DayTimeline::Column` strongly suggest that a previous implementation had some mechanism for client-side time rendering (likely using JavaScript or a Stimulus controller) which was later stubbed out. I noted how we've moved away from server-rendered time strings (like using `strftime` or `time_ago_in_words`) to sending raw timestamps (`<time>`), which allows the client-side, specifically `local-time` library, to render them according to the user's browser timezone.

**Detailed Design for Time Handling in the Application**

Okay, so I've got this figured out. The goal is to move all time rendering to the client-side for dynamic updates and to eliminate server-side timezone dependencies. Here's the plan:

First, `date_helpers.js` has a function `signedDifferenceInDays` that is the *perfect* tool for `local-time` to determine those calendar differences. If the browser's timezone is used within `date_helpers.js`, then we get the following from `signedDifferenceInDays(now, targetDate)`:

*   0: same day ("today!")
*   -1: yesterday!
*   -2 to -6: "2 days ago" to "6 days ago"
*   1: tomorrow!
*   2 or more: "in 2 days," etc.

Now, let's look at implementation.

1.  **Helper and Tag:** We need a Rails helper, `TimeHelper`, to generate the `<time>` tag. The name `local_datetime_tag` or `local_time_tag` (or whatever) sounds right, and we should use the existing `.local-time-value` CSS class. Let's make sure the helper is called `local_datetime_tag(datetime, style: :agoorago, **options)`

    module TimeHelper
      def local_datetime_tag(datetime, style: :agoorago, **attributes)
        return if datetime.blank?

        tag.time(
          datetime: datetime.utc.iso8601, # ISO8601 UTC timestamp!
          class: class_names("local-time-value", attributes.delete(:class)),
          data: {
            controller: "local-time",
            local_time_format_value: style,
            **attributes.delete(:data).to_h
          },
          **attributes
        )
      end

    The important thing is to ensure that the content inside `<time>` is *not* baked in on the server. We send the raw ISO8601 UTC timestamp, like `<time datetime="2025-01-22T17:30:00Z" ...></time>`. Javascript then populates the text content. This ensures no server timezone is baked in and the HTML can be cached! Use `.utc.iso8601` to be sure to have the correct timezone and a consistent output.

    *   For the server-rendered content, we *leave it empty* and let the Javascript fill it in. This avoids baking the server's time into the HTML, which is a big win.
    *   For dates (not timestamps), the server *should* pass them through as full timestamps (`.to_time.utc.iso8601`).

Okay, so I'm diving deep into this potential timezone issue. The initial assessment is promising – it looks like nothing in the core JavaScript or tests relies on old date formats, which is a good starting point. Now, let's systematically go through the codebase and identify any vulnerabilities.

Here is a place we need to review carefully, given that we are updating these date/times.

The big picture is about caching and timezones. My primary concern is that if any controller is rendering a `<time>` tag within a cached fragment, like a card, comment, notification, or even an access token, it might be baking in the server's timezone. This could happen if a user in one timezone views this, the view is cached, and then a user in a different timezone sees the *same* cached HTML. The result would be stale time information, based on the *original* user's timezone, leading to incorrect display for subsequent users.

Before the fix, this is what would happen: the server renders strings like "Added 5 minutes ago" or "Tuesday, January 21, 5:30 PM", which would be cached. User B, in a different timezone, would receive the server's timezone, rather than their own. After the fix, the server will *only* render a raw ISO timestamp: `<time datetime="2025-01-22T17:30:00Z" class="local-time-value" data-controller="local-time" data-local-time-style-value="agoorago"></time>`. The HTML is now identical for everyone! The browser will then do its job and convert the raw timestamp into words (or local time) in the user's *own* timezone.

To confirm all this, I'll need to create a test script or reproduce the issue via `bin/rails runner`. The plan is to:

1.  Demonstrate that the current code bakes server timezone strings into HTML, particularly in cached fragments. This includes using `strftime` and `time_ago_in_words`.
2.  Then, run the app in different timezones, like `America/Los_Angeles` and `Asia/Tokyo`, to verify that the rendered page is indeed showing the *server's* timezone rather than the browser's. This is the issue we're setting out to fix!

Right, so I was just going over some of the code, and I had a classic "d'oh!" moment. The fix, of course, is straightforward: We need to ensure that the Ruby code block within the heredoc is treated as a literal string. The easiest way to achieve this is to wrap the Ruby snippet with single quotes. That's the key to preventing the shell from getting involved prematurely.

**Testing Local Time Rendering in System Tests**

Okay, so I've noticed those timestamps in `test/fixtures/comments.yml`, specifically `logo_agreement_kevin` from `2.hours.ago` and `logo_agreement_jz` from `2.days.ago`. It's time to write a system test, `test/system/local_time_test.rb`, and get it running in Chrome. The crucial bit here is how we can use Chrome's CDP with `page.driver.browser.execute_cdp("Emulation.setTimezoneOverride", timezoneId: "America/New_York")` – or any other timezone like `Asia/Tokyo` – to directly test timezone rendering within the browser.

The key to remember is that `travel_to` on the Rails server only changes Ruby's `Time.current`, *not* the browser's `new Date()` object. This means, within the system tests, we have a few strategies. We can compute timestamps relative to `Time.current`, which will stay aligned with Chrome's wall clock (very useful for relative time tests). Or, we can test specific calendar offsets from `Time.current` in a specified timezone.

To be even more precise, here's the approach:

1.  Use `Time.current` in combination with a specific `ActiveSupport::TimeZone`, say "America/Los_Angeles".
    *   For timestamps earlier TODAY in "America/Los_Angeles", I can choose a time earlier than the current time in LA. If it's 15:00 in LA, I'd pick 13:00. Even if it's 00:30, using `Time.current - 5.minutes` is guaranteed to be today, in LA, and I can be confident of its formatted string.
    *   For YESTERDAY at 23:30 in "America/Los_Angeles", I'll use `(Time.current.in_time_zone("America/Los_Angeles") - 1.day).change(hour: 23, min: 30)`. This will be "yesterday", even if it's currently 01:00 in LA.
    *   For "5 days ago," I'll use `5.days.ago`.
    *   For "10 days ago," I'll use `10.days.ago.in_time_zone("America/Los_Angeles").strftime("%b %-d")`. I'll add `, %Y` if the year differs.
    *   To pick a timestamp for TOMORROW (auto-closing overnight), I'll use `(Time.current.in_time_zone("America/Los_Angeles") + 1.day).change(hour: 1, min: 0)`.
    *   For 3 days out, I can use `3.days.from_now`.
    *   To check cross-timezone day boundaries, I can set up a comment created at `Time.current.in_time_zone("Asia/Tokyo").beginning_of_day + 2.hours`. This would be 2 AM today in Tokyo, but YESTERDAY in Los Angeles. By visiting the card with Chrome first in "Asia/Tokyo", it should show "2:00 AM". Then, by changing Chrome's timezone to "America/Los_Angeles" (without server changes or cache clears), I should see the *same* comment now read "yesterday".

So, let's write `test/system/local_time_test.rb` and get cracking!

require "application_system_test_case"

class LocalTimeTest < ApplicationSystemTestCase
  include ActionView::RecordIdentifier

  setup do
    sign_in_as(users(:david))
    @card = cards(:logo)
  end

  teardown do
    page.driver.browser.execute_cdp("Emulation.setTimezoneOverride", timezoneId: "")
  end

  test "renders comment and card timestamps in the viewer's own timezone" do
    tz = "America/Los_Angeles"
    set_browser_timezone(tz)

    now_in_tz = Time.current.in_time_zone(tz)
    earlier_today = now_in_tz.hour >= 2 ? now_in_tz - 2.hours : now_in_tz.beginning_of_day + 1.minute
    last_night = (now_in_tz - 1.day).change(hour: 23, min: 30)
    five_days_ago = (now_in_tz - 5.days).change(hour: 12, min: 0)
    ten_days_ago = (now_in_tz - 10.days).change(hour: 12, min: 0)

    comment_today = @card.comments.create!(creator: users(:kevin), body: "Today comment", created_at: earlier_today)
    comment_yesterday = @card.comments.create!(creator: users(:kevin), body: "Yesterday comment", created_at: last_night)
    comment_five_days = @card.comments.create!(creator: users(:kevin), body: "Five days comment", created_at: five_days_ago)
    comment_older = @card.comments.create!(creator: users(:kevin), body: "Older comment", created_at: ten_days_ago)

    expected_today = earlier_today.strftime("%-l:%M %p").strip
    expected_older = ten_days_ago.year == now_in_tz.year ? ten_days_ago.strftime("%b %-d") : ten_days_ago.strftime("%b %-d, %Y")

    visit card_url(@card)

    within "##{dom_id(comment_today)}" do
      assert_selector "time.local-time-value", text: expected_today
    end

    within "##{dom_id(comment_yesterday)}" do
      assert_selector "time.local-time-value", text: /yesterday/i
    end

    within "##{dom_id(comment_five_days)}" do
      assert_selector "time.local-time-value", text: /5 days ago/i
    end

    within "##{dom_id(comment_older)}" do
      assert_selector "time.local-time-value", text: expected_older
    end
  end

  test "renders auto-closing notice as tomorrow overnight and in N days further out" do
    tz = "America/New_York"
    set_browser_timezone(tz)

    now_in_tz = Time.current.in_time_zone(tz)
    period = @card.auto_postpone_period

    # Auto-closing tomorrow in viewer's timezone
    overnight_clean_at = (now_in_tz + 1.day).change(hour: 2, min: 0)
    @card.update!(last_active_at: overnight_clean_at - period)

    visit card_url(@card)
    assert_selector "##{dom_id(@card, :closure_notice)}", text: "Moves to “Not Now” tomorrow if there’s no activity."

    # Auto-closing 3 days from now in viewer's timezone
    three_days_clean_at = (now_in_tz + 3.days).change(hour: 12, min: 0)
    @card.update!(last_active_at: three_days_clean_at - period)

    visit card_url(@card)
    assert_selector "##{dom_id(@card, :closure_notice)}", text: "Moves to “Not Now” in 3 days if there’s no activity."
  end

  test "same cached HTML renders differently across viewer timezones" do
    tokyo_tz = "Asia/Tokyo"
    la_tz = "America/Los_Angeles"

    # 2:00 AM today in Tokyo is always yesterday in Los Angeles (16-17h behind)
    tokyo_morning = Time.current.in_time_zone(tokyo_tz).beginning_of_day + 2.hours
    comment = @card.comments.create!(creator: users(:kevin), body: "Cross-timezone comment", created_at: tokyo_morning)

    set_browser_timezone(tokyo_tz)
    visit card_url(@card)
    within "##{dom_id(comment)}" do
      assert_selector "time.local-time-value", text: "2:00 AM"
    end

    set_browser_timezone(la_tz)
    visit card_url(@card)
    within "##{dom_id(comment)}" do
      assert_selector "time.local-time-value", text: /yesterday/i
    end
  end

  test "timestamps stay rendered after Turbo morph refresh" do
    set_browser_timezone("America/New_York")
    visit card_url(@card)

    assert_selector "turbo-cable-stream-source[connected]", visible: :all
    assert_no_selector "turbo-cable-stream-source:not([connected])", visible: :all

    @card.update!(title: "Updated title via broadcast")
    perform_enqueued_jobs only: Turbo::Streams::BroadcastStreamJob

    assert_selector "h1", text: "Updated title via broadcast", wait: 5
    all("time.local-time-value").each do |time_el|
      assert_not_equal "", time_el.text.strip
    end
  end

  private
    def set_browser_timezone(timezone_id)
      page.driver.browser.execute_cdp("Emulation.setTimezoneOverride", timezoneId: timezone_id)
    end
end
EOF

require "application_system_test_case"

class LocalTimeTest < ApplicationSystemTestCase
  include ActionView::RecordIdentifier

  setup do
    sign_in_as(users(:david))
    Current.user = users(:kevin)
    @card = cards(:logo)
  end

  teardown do
    page.driver.browser.execute_cdp("Emulation.setTimezoneOverride", timezoneId: "")
  end

  test "renders comment and card timestamps in the viewer's own timezone" do
    tz = "America/Los_Angeles"
    set_browser_timezone(tz)

    now_in_tz = Time.current.in_time_zone(tz)
    earlier_today = now_in_tz.hour >= 2 ? now_in_tz - 2.hours : now_in_tz.beginning_of_day + 1.minute
    last_night = (now_in_tz - 1.day).change(hour: 23, min: 30)
    five_days_ago = (now_in_tz - 5.days).change(hour: 12, min: 0)
    ten_days_ago = (now_in_tz - 10.days).change(hour: 12, min: 0)

    comment_today = @card.comments.create!(creator: users(:kevin), body: "Today comment", created_at: earlier_today)
    comment_yesterday = @card.comments.create!(creator: users(:kevin), body: "Yesterday comment", created_at: last_night)
    comment_five_days = @card.comments.create!(creator: users(:kevin), body: "Five days comment", created_at: five_days_ago)
    comment_older = @card.comments.create!(creator: users(:kevin), body: "Older comment", created_at: ten_days_ago)

    @card.update!(created_at: five_days_ago, last_active_at: earlier_today)

    expected_today = earlier_today.strftime("%-l:%M %p").strip
    expected_older = ten_days_ago.year == now_in_tz.year ? ten_days_ago.strftime("%b %-d") : ten_days_ago.strftime("%b %-d, %Y")

    visit card_url(@card)

    within "##{dom_id(@card, :meta)}" do
      assert_selector ".card__meta-text--added time.local-time-value", text: /5 days ago/i
      assert_selector ".card__meta-text--updated time.local-time-value", text: expected_today
    end

    within "##{dom_id(comment_today)}" do
      assert_selector "time.local-time-value", text: expected_today
    end

    within "##{dom_id(comment_yesterday)}" do
      assert_selector "time.local-time-value", text: /yesterday/i
    end

    within "##{dom_id(comment_five_days)}" do
      assert_selector "time.local-time-value", text: /5 days ago/i
    end

    within "##{dom_id(comment_older)}" do
      assert_selector "time.local-time-value", text: expected_older
    end
  end

  test "renders auto-closing notice as tomorrow overnight and in N days further out" do
    tz = "America/New_York"
    set_browser_timezone(tz)

    now_in_tz = Time.current.in_time_zone(tz)
    period = @card.auto_postpone_period

    # Auto-closing overnight (tomorrow in viewer's timezone)
    overnight_clean_at = (now_in_tz + 1.day).change(hour: 2, min: 0)
    @card.update!(last_active_at: overnight_clean_at - period)

    visit card_url(@card)
    assert_selector "##{dom_id(@card, :closure_notice)}", text: "Moves to “Not Now” tomorrow if there’s no activity."

    # Auto-closing 3 days from now in viewer's timezone
    three_days_clean_at = (now_in_tz + 3.days).change(hour: 12, min: 0)
    @card.update!(last_active_at: three_days_clean_at - period)

    visit card_url(@card)
    assert_selector "##{dom_id(@card, :closure_notice)}", text: "Moves to “Not Now” in 3 days if there’s no activity."
  end

  test "renders closed stamp and closure message in the viewer's own timezone" do
    closed_at = Time.utc(2025, 9, 13, 2, 0, 0) # Sep 12 10:00 PM in NY, Sep 13 11:00 AM in Tokyo
    @card.close(user: users(:david))
    @card.closure.update!(created_at: closed_at)

    set_browser_timezone("America/New_York")
    visit card_url(@card)
    assert_selector ".card__closed-date time.local-time-value", text: /Sep 12, 2025/i
    assert_selector ".card-perma__closure-message", text: /Completed by David on Sep 12, 2025\./

    set_browser_timezone("Asia/Tokyo")
    visit card_url(@card)
    assert_selector ".card__closed-date time.local-time-value", text: /Sep 13, 2025/i
    assert_selector ".card-perma__closure-message", text: /Completed by David on Sep 13, 2025\./
  end

  test "same cached HTML renders differently across viewer timezones" do
    tokyo_tz = "Asia/Tokyo"
    la_tz = "America/Los_Angeles"

    # A comment from 10 hours ago is always a different clock time in Tokyo vs LA,
    # and crosses midnight in whichever timezone had midnight in the last 10 hours.
    comment_time = 2.hours.ago
    comment = @card.comments.create!(creator: users(:kevin), body: "Cross-timezone comment", created_at: comment_time)

    set_browser_timezone(tokyo_tz)
    visit card_url(@card)
    tokyo_text = find("##{dom_id(comment)} time.local-time-value").text

    set_browser_timezone(la_tz)
    visit card_url(@card)
    la_text = find("##{dom_id(comment)} time.local-time-value").text

    assert_not_equal tokyo_text, la_text
    assert_equal expected_agoorago(comment_time, tokyo_tz), tokyo_text
    assert_equal expected_agoorago(comment_time, la_tz), la_text
  end

  test "renders access tokens and events timeline in the viewer's own timezone" do
    tz = "America/Chicago"
    set_browser_timezone(tz)

    token = users(:david).identity.access_tokens.create!(description: "Test CLI", permission: :read, created_at: Time.utc(2025, 1, 22, 19, 42, 0))
    visit my_access_tokens_url
    expected_token_time = token.created_at.in_time_zone(tz).strftime("%-m/%-d/%y, %-l:%M %p").strip
    assert_selector "tr", text: /Test CLI.*#{Regexp.escape(expected_token_time)}/

    event_time = Time.current.in_time_zone(tz).beginning_of_day + 9.hours + 15.minutes
    events(:layout_assignment_jz).update!(created_at: event_time)
    visit events_url
    assert_selector ".event__timestamp", text: event_time.strftime("%-l:%M %p").strip
  end

  test "timestamps stay rendered after Turbo morph refresh" do
    set_browser_timezone("America/New_York")
    visit card_url(@card)

    assert_selector "turbo-cable-stream-source[connected]", visible: :all
    assert_no_selector "turbo-cable-stream-source:not([connected])", visible: :all

    @card.update!(title: "Updated title via broadcast")
    perform_enqueued_jobs only: Turbo::Streams::BroadcastStreamJob

    assert_selector "h1", text: "Updated title via broadcast", wait: 5
    all("time.local-time-value").each do |time_el|
      assert_not_equal "", time_el.text.strip
    end
  end

  private
    def set_browser_timezone(timezone_id)
      page.driver.browser.execute_cdp("Emulation.setTimezoneOverride", timezoneId: timezone_id)
    end

    def expected_agoorago(time, tz)
      now = Time.current.in_time_zone(tz)
      target = time.in_time_zone(tz)
      days_diff = (target.to_date - now.to_date).to_i

      if days_diff == 0
        target.strftime("%-l:%M %p").strip
      elsif days_diff == -1
        "Yesterday" # CSS text-transform: capitalize
      else
        "#{days_diff.abs} days ago"
      end
    end
end
EOF
